en: Taal Volcano features a unique nested structure with an island volcano inside a crater lake inside a larger volcanic caldera.
Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental features a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only a few feet tall.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Pasig River in Manila is technically an estuary because its water flow direction reverses depending on the ocean tide.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Tuguegarao City in Cagayan frequently records the highest temperatures in the Philippines, often exceeding 40 degrees Celsius during the summer.
The Philippines holds the largest copper and gold deposits per square kilometer, making its land incredibly rich in natural minerals.
Apo Reef Natural Park in Mindoro is the largest contiguous coral reef system in the Philippines, hosting diverse marine biodiversity.
The San Juanico Bridge connects the islands of Leyte and Samar, featuring a distinctive harp-shaped design spanning over two kilometers.
The Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features exceptionally clear, deep blue water originating from a mysterious underwater cave system.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago, stretching an estimated halfway around the globe.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower portion subject to tidal influences.
